summary: Taikyo Tanigawa specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology, having studied at Koyasan University and completed a Ph.D. at Toyo University in 1994. He has held positions as associate professor and professor at Koyasan University, attested from 1980 through 2026.
Taion Satomi is a Buddhist studies scholar who graduated from Rissho University in 1933. He served as a professor at Minobusan Junior College, attested in 1972.

Taira Shidehara was an archaeology and history scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo from circa 1891 to 1896. He later held posts at the University of Tokyo (~1900–1906) and Tokyo University of Education (~1902–1906).

Tairyo Makita was a Buddhist studies and sinology scholar who studied at Bukkyo, Otani, and Kyoto universities. He was a professor at Kyoto University (1946; 1949–1976), Gifu Shotoku Gakuen University, and president of Saitama Institute of Technology (1997).
Tairyu Tsunoda is a Buddhist studies scholar. He served as a lecturer at Komazawa Junior College (attested 1995) and as a professor at Komazawa University (attested 2015).

Taisei Iwata is a Buddhist studies scholar. He held posts as a lecturer at Rissho University (attested 1984), professor at Otani University (attested 1996), and advisor at Minobusan University (attested 2026).
Taisen Deshimaru was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who studied under Kodo Sawaki from circa 1936 to 1965. He founded the Association Zen Internationale and La Gendronnière.

Taishu Tagami is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who studied at Komazawa University and earned a master's degree from the University of Tokyo. He held posts at Komazawa University and the Eastern Institute, attested in 1990.
Taishun Mibu was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who graduated from Taisho University in 1937. He later served as library director at Taisho University, attested in 1972.

Taitetsu Unno was a scholar of Buddhist studies, religion, and philosophy. He studied at UC Berkeley and the University of Tokyo, and served as Jill Ker Conway Professor Emeritus of Religion at Smith College (1971–1998).
Taitsu Kono is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Hanazono University and under Mumon Yamada (~1954–1988). He served as president of Hanazono University from circa 1993 to 2001.

Taixu was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied under Jing'an, Jichan, and Renshan Yang. He served as leader of Minnan Buddhist Institute (1927) and founded several institutions, including Wuchang Buddhist Institute and the World Fellowship of Buddhists.

Taizan Maezumi was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University, Soji-ji, SFSU, and under Hakujun Kuroda, Koryu Osaka, and Hakuun Ryoko Yasutani. He served as a priest at Zenshuji Soto Mission (1956) and founded ZCLA.
Tak Pui Sze is a scholar of sinology and religious studies who earned a PhD at the University of British Columbia under the supervision of Jinhua Chen, attested in 2012.

Taka Yanagisawa was a history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Japan Women's University. She served as Director of the Department of Fine Arts at the Tokyo National Research Institute for Cultural Properties.
Takahiko Kameyama is a Buddhist studies scholar. In 2015, he was attested as a professor at the Institute of Buddhist Studies and as a part-time lecturer at Ryukoku University.
Takahiko Sato is a Buddhist studies scholar who served as a professor at Koyasan University, attested in 2015 and 2026.

Takahiro Kato is an Indology and philosophy scholar who completed his doctoral dissertation at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg in 2011. He holds posts as professor at the University of Tokyo and at the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute, attested in 2026.
Takako Abe is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who served as a lecturer (attested 2013–2017) and faculty member (attested 2026) at Taisho University.

Takamaro Shigaraki was a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at Ryukoku University. He served as professor and president of Ryukoku University (1989–1995) and chairman of Bukkyo Dendo Kyokai (1995–2008; ~2010–2014), and founded Kōmyōji.
